product_brief: Microsoft's customer-managed, single-tenant, highly available HSM service on Marvell LiquidSecurity hardware. Each cluster has three HSMs reached through a private endpoint, and Microsoft states FIPS 140-3 Level 3. The cited pages name no post-quantum capability.
pqc_capability_description: Azure Cloud HSM is a customer-managed, single-tenant HSM service on Marvell LiquidSecurity hardware security modules. Microsoft's FAQ lists PKCS#11, SSL/TLS offload, certificate authority private key protection, transparent data encryption, and document and code signing as supported uses, and names no post-quantum algorithm, firmware or roadmap, so whether the service supports post-quantum algorithms is not stated on the cited pages.
fips_validated: Microsoft states the service's HSMs are validated to meet FIPS 140-3 Level 3 and gives no certificate number on the cited pages.
regulatory_status: FIPS 140-3 Level 3, eIDAS (Austrian scheme), PCI, PCI 3DS

evidence.Hardware: Azure Cloud HSM uses Marvell LiquidSecurity hardware security modules.
evidence.FIPS Validated: Yes, Azure Cloud HSM offers HSMs that are validated to meet FIPS 140-3 Level 3 standards.
evidence.Product Brief: It's a customer-managed, single-tenant, highly available service that complies with industry standards.
evidence.Supported uses: Azure Cloud HSM supports various applications, including PKCS#11, offloading of Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) or Transport Layer Security (TLS) processing, certificate authority (CA) private key protection, and transparent data encryption (TDE). It also supports document and code signing.
evidence.License: You incur an hourly fee for each Azure Cloud HSM cluster, which consists of three nodes.
evidence.Regulatory status: Yes, Azure Cloud HSM supports eIDAS compliance under the Austrian scheme.
